tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrap did the bulk namespace rewrite, triage, and TODO seeding; MIGRATION-MAPPING had 9 rows all resolved.
Turn 17 the agent fetched the lifecycle anchor to diagnose the Suspending compile error.
Turn 23 reported PASS (residue, build 0 WUI warnings, smoke launch alive pid 17892, visible-text fidelity).

tool_limitations.limitation: The lifecycle anchor covered only activation (OnLaunched/OnActivated/AppInstance) and said nothing about suspend/resume, so it did not directly answer the Suspending compile error.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add suspend/resume guidance to the lifecycle anchor.

failed_apis.why_tried: Carried over verbatim from the UWP App.xaml.cs SuspensionManager template.
failed_apis.root_cause: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application has no Suspending/Resuming events; desktop apps are not OS-suspended.
failed_apis.fix: Removed this.Suspending += OnSuspending and the OnSuspending handler; saved state via window.Closed += async (_,_) => await SuspensionManager.SaveAsync().

doc_errors.wrong: Section titled 'Application Lifecycle and Activation' covers only activation; omits suspend/resume entirely.
doc_errors.correct: Application.Suspending/Resuming do not exist in WinUI 3 desktop; save state on Window.Closed instead.

special_apis.special_handling: UWP suspension save/restore maps to saving on Window.Closed and restoring in OnLaunched; there is no OS suspend event.

errors_encountered.error: CS1061 'App' does not contain a definition for 'Suspending'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application lacks the UWP Suspending event.
errors_encountered.fix: Replace Suspending subscription with window.Closed save handler.

errors_encountered.error: CS8803/CS0106/CS1022 (top-level statements / orphaned members) in App.xaml.cs
errors_encountered.root_cause: Dev-agent's edit removed the OnSuspending wiring but left the old OnNavigationFailed + OnSuspending methods stranded after the class closing brace.
errors_encountered.fix: Second edit deleted the orphaned methods so the file had a single well-formed class.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Build failed on Suspending event (CS1061), then a follow-up edit left orphaned methods causing CS8803/CS0106/CS1022.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Skill lifecycle anchor never told the agent the UWP suspend/resume model is gone, so the agent had to discover and improvise the Window.Closed replacement at build-error time, and its large hand edit was error-prone.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent inferred Window.Closed as the save hook and cleaned up the stray methods on a third pass.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Add suspend/resume to the lifecycle anchor AND seed an inline TODO on Suspending/Resuming via unsupported-api-inventory.json so the agent is routed to the pattern before building.

missing_tooling.need: A pre-build signal flagging Application.Suspending/Resuming as having no WinUI 3 equivalent.
missing_tooling.would_have_saved: The CS1061 build failure and the follow-on botched edit (turns 16-22).
